body.value: The first four seasons were about establishing rules, rivalries, and rituals. No one knew what they were building — just that they wanted to keep playing. The NFL itself was in a golden age: Brady, Manning, and LaDainian Tomlinson were reshaping football. This league was figuring out who it was.

headline.value: The Bell Cow Runs the League

body.value: Shaun Alexander. LaDainian Tomlinson. Adrian Peterson. Chris Johnson. The five seasons from 2005 to 2009 were defined by dominant rushing attacks — and managers who built rosters around a single backfield star. In the NFL, the ground game ruled. In this league, bell cows made dynasties.

When the keeper rules took hold, everything changed. Drafting became about the future as much as the present. Managers began hoarding young talent, protecting emerging stars, and building multi-year rosters. The league started rewarding patience and planning over luck and reactivity. Some managers adapted. Others were left behind.

headline.value: Speed, Receivers, and the New Game

body.value: Patrick Mahomes. Alvin Kamara. Davante Adams. Justin Jefferson. Josh Allen. The NFL became a pass-first, points-everywhere league — and this one followed. Zero-RB strategies, TE premiums, and receiver kingdoms replaced the old bell-cow playbook. The managers who adapted to the new game are the ones still competing for titles.
